headline: High: Langflow’s broad filesystem/network defaults can amplify Botpress outputs into data leakage and unsafe downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a chatbot/agent builder, and Langflow can chain multiple agents with files and flow inputs as shared surfaces. That creates a plausible path where Botpress-generated content is fed into Langflow nodes and treated as instructions. The interaction is documented only indirectly, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Botpress outputs are copied into a Langflow flow node without provenance checks, injection risk exists.
IF Langflow chains Botpress output into another agent prompt, the content can be reinterpreted as instructions.
mitigations: Add a strict delimiter and instruction/data separator in the flow.
Require human review before any Botpress text is reused as a prompt.
Disable automatic chaining from Botpress outputs into agent nodes.
Log and flag any prompt-like tokens in Botpress outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between Botpress and Langflow nodes.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Botpress is open-source and Langflow explicitly reads/writes server filesystem files and handles flow inputs/intermediate outputs plus per-flow credentials. If Botpress content is placed into Langflow, default broad egress and server-side storage can expose sensitive flow data to external model providers or HTTP services. The shared workspace path is plausible and the blast radius can include secrets.
conditions: IF Botpress content includes secrets or customer data and is imported into Langflow flows, leakage risk exists.
IF Langflow flows call external model providers or HTTP services with that content, exfiltration can occur.
mitigations: Remove secrets from any Botpress-to-Langflow handoff.
Restrict Langflow flows to local-only providers for the pair.
Store credentials outside Langflow where possible.
Audit uploaded files and intermediate outputs before execution.
requires-engineering: add per-flow data-loss prevention and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, while Langflow can execute shell, spawn subprocesses, write the filesystem, and run unsandboxed Python by default. Even though Botpress itself shows no write or network egress, the pair still overlaps on mutable server-side resources through Langflow, making conflicting writes and environment changes dangerous in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same server filesystem, concurrent writes can collide.
IF Botpress package installation affects the same runtime used by Langflow, environment drift can occur.
mitigations: Separate Botpress and Langflow into different containers.
Mount distinct writable directories for each agent.
Pin package versions and disable ad hoc installs during shared runs.
Run Langflow code components in a sandbox.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow is designed to chain multiple agents and wire tools into flow nodes, so Botpress outputs can become authoritative inputs downstream. If Botpress emits incorrect or prompt-shaped content, Langflow may propagate it into actions or model calls without verification. That makes cascading errors likely in default flow designs, with potentially irreversible downstream effects.
conditions: IF a Langflow flow uses Botpress output as a node input without validation, errors cascade.
IF downstream Langflow nodes trigger external actions, incorrect Botpress content can cause real-world impact.
mitigations: Insert a validation node between Botpress and any action node.
Require schema checks on Botpress outputs.
Use confidence thresholds before downstream execution.
Keep Botpress outputs read-only unless verified.
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between flow nodes.

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress documentation here does not specify residency or retention, while Langflow stores per-flow credentials and intermediate outputs server-side and can send data to external providers. That creates a compliance mismatch risk for regulated data classes, but the exact breach depends on deployment and data class, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed in Langflow flows, retention and residency must be checked.
IF Botpress and Langflow are deployed under different compliance regimes, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it into either agent.
Disable storage of regulated fields in Langflow stores.
Review retention settings for flow inputs and outputs.
Use region-locked providers only.
requires-engineering: document a shared compliance boundary and DPA.
